claims.text: The proposed alloy is equiatomic Hf-Mo-Ta-Ti-Zr.
The approach requires oxygen content below 0.2 wt%.
SPS at 1200-1300°C followed by HPT or severe plastic deformation can produce the intended nanocrystalline microstructure.
HPT can reduce the grain size to below 1 μm.
The proposed processing route will promote B2-phase precipitation.
The desired microstructure consists of coherent nanoscale B2 precipitates in a disordered BCC matrix.
Grain boundaries in the proposed nanocrystalline alloy act as dislocation sources and sinks.
B2 precipitates produce Orowan strengthening and dislocation pinning, thereby increasing yield strength.
Nanocrystalline grains and coherent interfaces enable multiple slip systems and dislocation cross-slip, thereby improving room-temperature ductility.
Replacing heavier elements such as Ta or Hf with lighter elements reduces alloy density.
The proposed elemental substitution maintains solid-solution strengthening.
The proposed alloy can achieve a yield strength above 1.2 GPa.
The proposed alloy can achieve tensile elongation above 10% at room temperature.
The proposed Hf-Mo-Ta-Ti-Zr alloy has lower density than baseline HfNbTaTiZr.
Baseline HfNbTaTiZr has a density of approximately 11.5 g/cm³.
Baseline HfNbTaTiZr has a room-temperature yield strength of approximately 0.8 GPa.
Baseline HfNbTaTiZr has room-temperature ductility below 5%.
The approach is applicable only when Mo content is between 15 and 25 at%.
The approach is applicable only when the Hf/Zr atomic ratio is between 0.8 and 1.2.
The approach is not applicable above 600°C because the B2 phase may decompose.

contradictions.description: The density strategy is described as replacing or reducing heavy Ta or Hf, but the explicitly proposed equiatomic Hf-Mo-Ta-Ti-Zr composition retains both Ta and Hf at nominally equal proportions.

The predicted outcome requires only an unspecified density reduction, whereas the experiment declares any reduction below 15% falsifying. An improvement smaller than 15% would therefore satisfy the stated prediction but fail the stated falsification criterion.
